disease: Neurodevelopmental disorder with congenital cardiac defects and variable renal and ocular abnormalities

messages.content: You are a clinical geneticist. You are given evidence about one rare disease and a cohort of patients described by HPO terms. Exactly one patient has the disease. Use only that evidence as your knowledge of the disease. Be explicit about which findings in the report drove each placement, and about findings that argue against it.

[1] NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH CONGENITAL CARDIAC DEFECTS ...
https://omim.org/entry/621474
A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that neurodevelopmental disorder with congenital cardiac defects and variable renal and ocular abnormalities (NEDCRO) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KDM2B gene (609078) on chromosome 12q24.

https://www.omim.org/entry/609078

(2023) identified a de novo heterozygous c.1912G-A transition (c.1912G-A, NM_032590.4) in the KDM2B gene, resulting in a gly638-to-ser (G638S) substitution at a highly ...

[3] Neurodevelopmental disorder with congenital cardiac defects ...
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/1896179
Atrial septal defect (ASD) is a congenital abnormality of the interatrial septum that enables blood flow between the left and right atria via the interatrial septum.

[4] KDM2B-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case-Series ...
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41457890/
This case series reinforces the consistent phenotype of KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and highlights ocular and dermatologic manifestations as recurring features in affected individuals.

[5] Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder ...
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36322151/
Purpose: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in the epigenetic machinery are an emerging cause of neurodevelopment disorders (NDDs). Lysine-demethylase 2B (KDM2B) encodes an epigenetic regulator and mouse models suggest an important role during development.

[6] Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder ...
https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S109836002200942X
We set out to determine whether KDM2B variants are associated with NDD. Through international collaborations, we collected data on individuals with heterozygous KDM2B variants. We applied methylation arrays on peripheral blood DNA samples to determine a KDM2B associated epigenetic signature.

Task: rank the five most likely patients, most likely first, with a probability for each (they need not sum to one). For each, say which findings in the report support the placement and which argue against it, counting recorded absences as evidence; keep each to one or two sentences. Then say what the report lacked that would have made you more confident.

ranking.for: Matches the core tetrad implied by the condition name, presenting with neurodevelopmental delay/intellectual disability, congenital cardiac involvement (mitral regurgitation), a renal malformation (pelvic kidney), and ocular defects (astigmatism and hypermetropia).
ranking.against: Lacks specific structural septal defects such as atrial septal defect mentioned in the disease literature, presenting instead with mitral regurgitation.

ranking.for: Presents with severe global developmental delay and prominent congenital cardiac abnormalities including bicuspid aortic valve and aortic valve stenosis.
ranking.against: Explicitly tested negative for atrial septal defect, and lacks any documented renal or ocular abnormalities.

ranking.for: Features neurodevelopmental delay along with multiple ocular abnormalities (myopia, ptosis, and esotropia).
ranking.against: Has confirmed absences of major congenital heart defects, including secundum atrial septal defect, ventricular septal defect, and patent ductus arteriosus, with no renal abnormalities reported.

ranking.for: Displays neurodevelopmental deficits (intellectual disability, autism, motor delay) combined with ocular involvement (strabismus and hypermetropia).
ranking.against: Completely lacks documented congenital cardiac defects and renal anomalies.

ranking.for: Exhibits global developmental delay, intellectual disability, and an ocular-associated finding (lacrimal duct atresia).
ranking.against: Lacks congenital cardiac defects, renal abnormalities, and other typical ocular manifestations.

rounds.what_the_report_lacked: The report provided minimal phenotypic detail beyond the broad disease name and general category mentions; detailed frequencies of specific cardiac defects (e.g., whether mitral valve disease or specific septal defects predominate), typical renal phenotypes, and definitive ocular findings would have provided stronger discriminatory power.

ranking.for: Presents the complete syndromic constellation described for NEDCRO, including neurodevelopmental impairment (intellectual disability, motor delay), a congenital/valvular cardiac defect (mitral regurgitation), a structural renal abnormality (pelvic kidney), and ocular anomalies (astigmatism, hypermetropia).
ranking.against: Common dysmorphic cranial/facial features often tracked in neurodevelopmental syndromes are documented as absent.

ranking.for: Features severe global developmental delay alongside congenital cardiac abnormalities (bicuspid aortic valve, aortic valve stenosis).
ranking.against: Lacks the characteristic renal and ocular involvement, and specifically tested negative for an atrial septal defect.

ranking.for: Presents with neurodevelopmental delay and prominent ocular abnormalities (myopia, ptosis, esotropia).
ranking.against: Lacks renal findings and congenital cardiac defects are specifically documented as absent (including atrial septal defect, VSD, and PDA).
